vsm1.6:2.3: It is not possible to render such associative and alliterative derivations of meaning into English. They have nothing to do with the historical development of words, and their purpose is purely mnemonic.
vsm1.6:25.3: This does not imply what we, now, might suppose. See the description of “brain” in VIII.126 and especially VIII.136. What is meant is perhaps that he might get a cold or catarrh.
vsm1.6:35.2: Reference back to §19 requires sabhāvato upalakkhati rather than sabhāvato vavaṭṭhāpeti, but so the readings have it.
vsm1.6:35.3: Vaṇita—“inflated”: glossed by Vism-mhṭ with sūna (swollen). Not in PED in this sense.
